newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends mostly up on crushers, commercials.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends mostly up on crushers, commercials.

text.p: WCE canola ended mostly higher on commercial and crusher buying, traders said.

"Crushers bought November. Commercials bought August and locals sold across the board," a trader said. Japanese exporters bought August at the close while longs liquidated July positions. November WCE futures crush margin fell to -5.79 Thursday from -0.66 Friday. About 190 Sep-Nov spread at $2. Volume was 2,400 lots, or 48,000 tonnes, with 100 hedges.
July closed $0.90 lower at $355.10 after setting a new low of $354.50. November closed $1.90 higher at $335.10.
July flax rose $2 to end at $330.50 on commercial short covering linked to low stocks, traders said, and November flax fell $1.50 to $284 on farmer selling.
Oats and feed peas did not trade.

July western barley ended down $1.90 at $119.10 on commercial liquidation after it set a new low of $119. Alberta Wheat Pool sold October down $1.20 to $122.80 after it touched a new low at $122.10, traders said.
Commercials bought 100 October feed wheat late down $1.20 to $148.60 from locals after it set a new low at $147.50, sources said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, peas.)
